name: Familial Cavitary Optic Disc Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Familial Cavitary Optic Disc Anomaly Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic cavitary excavation of the optic disc on ophthalmologic examination
Positive family history of similar optic disc anomalies consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Visual field defects consistent with optic nerve dysfunction
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) or fundus imaging confirming optic disc cavitation
Exclusion of other optic neuropathies or congenital optic disc anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of optic disc cavitation confirmed by imaging plus positive family history and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on ophthalmologic imaging and family history; genetic testing may be supportive if causative mutations identified.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cavitary excavation of the optic disc
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic morphological feature seen on fundoscopic exam and imaging

occasional.symptomName: Mild optic nerve dysfunction without significant vision loss
searchTerms: optic nerve issues without vision loss

imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing cavitary excavation of optic nerve head
Fundus photography demonstrating optic disc anomalies
Visual field testing revealing characteristic defects
genetic: Potential autosomal dominant inheritance pattern; specific gene mutations not well characterized
other: Family history consistent with inherited optic disc anomaly

distinguishingFeatures: Coloboma involves a full-thickness defect of optic disc with associated chorioretinal coloboma
Distinct funnel-shaped excavation with surrounding peripapillary pigmentary changes
Small optic disc with reduced nerve fiber layer thickness
Often associated with midline brain abnormalities

redFlags: Unilateral optic disc swelling with pain
Signs of increased intraocular pressure or glaucoma
